newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSEE head sees French H1 growth rate 2 to 2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSEE head sees French H1 growth rate 2 to 2.5 pct.

text.p: French economic growth should accelerate to an annual rate of two to 2.5 percent in the second half of 1996, Paul Champsaur, head of national statistics institute INSEE told the National Assembly finance committee.
Champsaur was heard by the finance committee on Wednesday, and his comments were reported in committee minutes released on Thursday.

French gross domestic product fell 0.4 percent in the second quarter from the first quarter after rising 1.1 percent in the first. The government said the economy was recovering, and it expected full-year growth of 1.3 percent.
The minutes said Champsaur based his forecast on a recovery in trade in industrial goods in Europe and to the delayed effects of a recovery in the property market.
The forecast also assumed some optimism on the part of companies whose mediocre outlook, he was quoted as saying, contradicted the current situation for consumer spending.
Continued recovery beyond the end of 1996 would require at least minimum internal demand.
Risks came less from consumer spending -- since new increases in purchasing power would support this -- than from business investment, which was stagnant.
The minutes said "one should not underestimate the investment effort which would be required to reattain growth potential, estimated at 2.5 percent, and all the more so to catch up on lost ground."
